name: under_target_no_split
why: a segment already at or under the phoneme target is returned unchanged.

name: clause_split_at_comma_then_word_boundary

input.text: This is clause one, and this is clause two which is a bit longer than the first.

expect.text: and this is clause two which
is a bit longer than the

why: the first clause (up to and including the comma) already fits the target; the long second clause has no more clause punctuation, so it falls through to greedy word-boundary packing. Offsets tile the source with no gaps.

name: clause_split_at_semicolon

input.text: This is clause one; and this is clause two which is a bit longer than the first.

expect.text: and this is clause two which
is a bit longer than the

why: semicolons split the same way commas do.

name: pure_word_boundary_split_no_punctuation

input.text: one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve thirteen fourteen

why: no clause punctuation anywhere, so the whole thing is packed greedily word by word up to the target; each inter-word gap is folded into the end of the preceding piece so the pieces still tile the source.

name: single_giant_word_over_limit_fixed_width_split
why: a single 'word' with no whitespace to split on and a phoneme count over the hard limit is cut at a fixed character width, recursively, until every piece fits; spec/chunking.md calls this the should-be-impossible backstop.

name: word_boundary_split_many_short_words

input.text: alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa lambda mu nu xi omicron pi

why: greedy packing takes as many whole words as fit under the target on each group, never fewer than it could.

name: repeated_run_no_spaces_fixed_width
why: a whitespace-free run over the limit is halved recursively regardless of where 'words' would conventionally be; every piece lands at exactly the limit or under.

name: multiple_clause_marks_then_word_boundary_on_the_remainder
why: comma, semicolon and colon all split; the final clause has no internal punctuation and no spaces, so it falls to the fixed-width backstop, still tiling the source.

name: doc_020_style_unpunctuated_excerpt_splits_and_tiles

input.text: The Time Traveller (for so it will be convenient to speak of him) was expounding a recondite matter to us His grey eyes shone and twinkled, and his usually pale face was flushed and animated The fire burnt brightly, and the soft radiance of the incandescent lights in the lilies of silver caught the bubbles that flashed and passed in our glasses

expect.text: The Time Traveller (for so it will be convenient to speak of
him) was expounding a recondite matter to us His grey eyes
and his usually pale face was flushed and animated The fire
and the soft radiance of the incandescent lights in the
lilies of silver caught the bubbles that flashed and passed

why: this is the opening of spec/eval/corpus/020.txt (role 'unpunctuated'), which arrives from segment.ts as one giant Segment; the mix of a couple of commas and long punctuation-free stretches exercises both the clause and word-boundary paths in one input. First piece starts at 0, last piece ends at 346 (the input's length), and every piece.end equals the next piece.start: the offsets tile the source exactly. A dedicated integration test (core.test.ts) re-runs the full doc against the real vendored phonemizer.
